cards.text: Friend, John is telling what God showed him in a vision (Revelation 1:1). He sees an angel coming down from heaven with a key, holding a great chain in his hand. I bet somebody's about to get locked up.

cards.question: The angel coming down from heaven holds the key to the ___.

cards.text: The angel seizes the dragon, that ancient serpent. It's the same dragon John saw hurled down to earth earlier in his vision (Revelation 12:9).

cards.question: John says the dragon the angel seizes has two more names. What are they?

cards.text: Then the angel binds him for a thousand years. FOUR names this guy has, friend, and I've only got two, one of them carved on my handle.

cards.question: The angel has the key to the Abyss and the dragon bound with a great chain. Where does the angel throw the dragon?

cards.text: The angel shuts the Abyss and seals it over him. I spent years shut in a junk drawer, friend, but at least mine popped open every time somebody needed TAPE.

cards.question: Why is the Abyss shut and sealed over the dragon?

answers.text: So he cannot deceive the nations
So he cannot reach the heavens
So he cannot harm the angels

cards.question: Once the thousand years are complete, the dragon stays sealed in the Abyss for good.

cards.text: Then John sees thrones, and those seated on them have been given authority to judge. He also sees the souls of people who had been beheaded.

cards.question: Why had the people John sees been beheaded?

answers.text: For their service in the temple
For their defense of the city

cards.text: John keeps looking at that scene. Earlier in his vision, he saw a beast rising out of the sea, and people were required to take its mark (Revelation 13:1, 16-17).

cards.question: Along with those souls, John sees people who had not worshiped the beast or received its mark.
What happens to those souls and to the ones who had not worshiped the beast?

answers.text: They come to life and reign with Christ
They rest under the altar a while longer
They stand guard over the sealed Abyss

cards.text: And the rest of the dead? John says they don't come back to life until the thousand years are complete.

cards.question: The ones who come to life and reign with Christ for the thousand years? John calls that the first ___.

cards.text: Then John says, "Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection!" Blessed AND holy, friend, that's a double batch.

cards.question: The second death has power over those who share in the first resurrection.
What will those who share in the first resurrection be as they reign with Christ?

answers.text: Priests of God and of Christ
Guards at the gates of the city

cards.text: When the thousand years are complete, Satan is released from his prison. A THOUSAND years locked up, friend, and he goes back to the same old job: deceiving the nations in the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog.

cards.question: Satan deceives the nations of Gog and Magog. What is he gathering them for?
John says the number of that gathered army is like the ___ of the seashore.

cards.text: That army marches across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounds the camp of the saints and the beloved city. And I used to think a junk drawer full of rubber bands was crowded.

cards.question: Satan's army surrounds the camp of the saints and the beloved city. Then what happens to that army?

answers.text: Fire comes down from heaven and consumes them
The saints march out and drive them away
They turn around and run back home

cards.text: Then the devil, the one who deceived them, is thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur. A thousand years locked up, friend, and the big comeback lasts about THREE verses.
And he's not the first one in there. The beast and the false prophet, who did signs for the beast (Revelation 19:20), had already been thrown in.

cards.question: John says the devil, the beast and the false prophet will be tormented there for a thousand years and then it ends.

cards.text: Then John sees a great white throne and the One seated on it. And something flees from His presence.

cards.question: What flees from the presence of the One seated on the great white throne?

cards.text: John sees the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books are opened. Great AND small, friend. Nobody sleeps through this one.

cards.question: One of the books opened before the throne has a name: the Book of ___.
How are the dead judged before the great white throne?

answers.text: By their deeds recorded in the books
By the gifts they bring to the throne
By the land they were born in

cards.text: Then John sees where those dead come from. The sea gives up its dead.

cards.question: The sea gives up its dead, and ___ and ___ give up their dead too.

cards.text: Then Death and Hades themselves are thrown into the lake of fire. After years in a junk drawer waiting to get tossed out, I never thought I'd CHEER for something getting thrown away.

cards.question: John calls the lake of fire the second death.
At the great white throne, who is thrown into the lake of fire?

answers.text: Anyone not written in the Book of Life
Anyone who rose up out of the sea
Anyone who stood before the throne

findings.problem: The opening card deliberately withholds what the key opens, and nothing earlier lets the baker reason out “Abyss” rather than another place. The blank asks for unseen wording from verse 1 instead of a meaning supported by the earlier cards.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The earlier cards say nothing about the army's number or develop a seashore comparison. With sand, waves and stones all able to suggest a large quantity, the baker must guess the unseen wording of John's simile.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 11 establishes only that books are opened at the judgment. It gives no clue that distinguishes the name “Book of Life” from “Book of Law” or “Book of Kings,” so the blank tests an unseen name rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Card 14 mentions only the sea giving up its dead. Neither Death nor Hades has been introduced in this role, so the baker cannot reason out the two blanks and must guess the wording of verse 13.
